needs_you.why: What the cheat menu's Unlock the map should open in each game; how quicksave and quickload work on a controller; and the two widescreen looks (the score box corner, Keen 5's yellow map filler).

Phones and app stores know an app by a package name that can never change once it is published. It is org.megarocket.app for now; say if you want another before anything is released.

milestones.text: Keen Dreams now has every display option Keen 1-6 have (native resolution, smooth motion, the wide view), drawn from its own draw list with every picture proven identical to the original's, and the Reveal secrets cheat with its 20 secrets. With that, Keen Dreams matches Keen 1-6 in menus, controls, cheats and extras

The launcher answers the controller's buttons (A or Start plays, B goes back): Godot's own menu actions held no controller buttons. Keen Dreams' secrets list is written (20 secrets from the official solution text and the level data), ready for the Reveal secrets cheat once Dreams' new drawing lands

Keen Dreams catches up with Keen 1-6: the cheats (a Cheat keycap in its panel: God mode, infinite ammo and lives, no clipping, jump, slow motion, freeze enemies, free items, extra lives, skip level, level select), quicksave and quickload (F8/F9), the Mode row, touch controls, and the fitted loading times now apply in play. Keen 1-3 can play Keen 4-5's music, a track per level

Menus: every game's main menu in one modern order in its own style (Resume, New Game, Load, Save, Options, Cheats, High Scores, Extras, Quit), a pause menu in Keen 1-3, Options tidied to Display, Sound, Controls, Gameplay; Keen Dreams' panel reordered with text keycaps. Keen 1-3 can use Keen 4-6's sound effects (from your own Keen 4 or 5)

Controls: one set of keys and controller buttons for all seven games, changed from each game's own menus (Keen 1-3's Options windows, Keen 4-6's watch cards, Keen Dreams' control panel); two keys per action, a countdown while it waits for your key, reset to defaults; the old Keyboard Commands screens replaced

Speed: Keen 4-6 now run 3.5-5 times faster than real time where they barely kept up (the sound and play slowed in Keen 4), every picture unchanged; Keen 1-3: the Keyboard Commands window can be left again, one-button fire uses your own jump and pogo keys, no white trail on the Cheats page

Reveal secrets cheat in Keen 1-6: 194 secrets from the official hint sheets, the wiki and walkthroughs, plus every hidden stash the level data shows, each checked by eye; a check confirms no hidden item is left out
Keen Dreams' gameplay proven against the original's code: every level of v1.00 and v1.93 played through ReflectionHLE alongside Megarocket, all objects identical on every frame
Answer keys for the secrets in Keen 1, 2, 5 and 6 (Keen 3 and 4 earlier), every guide-documented secret pinned to its place in the level data, for the coming Reveal secrets cheat
Keen Dreams plays from the launcher: both releases, its text-mode start screens drawn by Megarocket, its settings, high scores and saves kept between sessions
Quicksave and quickload in Keen 1-6 (Keen 1-3: F7/F9, working even after dying; Keen 4-6: F5/F9), asking first unless turned off, on in Enhanced
Keen 4-6 now keep your settings, high scores and saved games between sessions (they were being lost when the game closed)
Windows and messages over widescreen sit in the middle of the screen, also at a map's edge

Keen Maker, a first working preview: pick a Keen 1-6 game and level, paint with the game's own tiles, move Keen's start, undo, and press Play to try the level straight away; saves go to Megarocket's own folder, never the game's

Keen 4-6 get native resolution, smooth motion and widescreen: every gameplay picture of every built-in demo (34,633) redrawn and checked against the original's; the score box stays put in its corner; the status window opens over the wide view; menus and other screens sit in the bevelled frame over the game's own tiled backdrop
Map builder groundwork: every level of all seven games can be read and written back byte for byte, and a level changed by the builder loads in Keen 1-6

Playtest fixes for Keen 1-3: no stray pictures before the intro, the map opens wide straight away, the camera never shows past the level's edge, one-key fire on by default, the frame and backdrop on every 4:3 screen, a Quit button and F11 for fullscreen everywhere
Bug-fix toggles: the first five fixes in Keen 1-5's menus (on by default, Classic turns them off), each checked against the original behaviour; Keen 6's copy-protection question can be switched off
Keen 1-3 pictures can now be drawn without the old graphics card: every gameplay picture matches the original's, the base for native resolution, smooth motion and widescreen
Level select in Keen 1-6's cheat menus, and the original cheat codes listed where players can find them

Cheats in Keen 1-6, from each game's own menus: god mode, infinite ammo and lives, no clipping, jump cheat, slow motion, freeze enemies, free items, extra lives, skip level; the original cheat codes still work
Megarocket's own Options inside Keen 1-6's menus (Mode, Display, Sound, Controls), drawn in each game's own style
The launcher's new look: EGA colours, the original pixel font, a starfield and the rocket
Keen Dreams runs in Megarocket: its engine ported and checked piece by piece; both releases boot to the title
Keen 4-6 parity review done: every remaining difference checked; none is a game-logic bug
Keen 6 level sessions running against your v1.0 original: level 4 proven; v1.0's own texts (“Keen hungily enters”) read from your executable
Keen 4 levels 2 and 4 and Keen 5 level 2 proven against the original; a new check holds each picture to the original's timing so the game's own logic can be proven through deaths and restarts
The original's memory manager modelled and proven against its own memory map (Keen 4 and 5)
Keen 4 level 1 proven against the original, picture for picture
Keen 4-6: every level recorded in the original; random seed and level fade-in now follow the original
Phones: on-screen touch controls for every game (hidden while a pad is used), and Back works as Escape
On Android: Export for Android on the computer, one import on the phone, and Keen 1 to 6 all start and play on the emulator
Android: the app builds from the same project and opens to the launcher on the phone emulator, sound chip loaded, sized for a phone
While playing: losing focus or unplugging the pad pauses the game; music and effects volumes from the settings
Keen 3 proven: all 16 levels match the original to the refresh
Keen 4's title fizzle and story screen drawn as the original draws them (read from the reconstructed Keen 4 source)
Every launcher message says what happened and what to do next; a log file, its path on screen
Launcher: each game's own title screen on its tile, a phone-width carousel, a how-to page, Add a folder (remembered), one copy at a time; pads play
Playable: the launcher finds all seven games and starts Keen 1-6 in a window, in real time with the keyboard (no sound yet)
Keen 4 in Megarocket boots like the original: intro, credits, title and the first demo match the DOSBox recording picture for picture
Keen 4, 5 and 6 engine ported: all twelve built-in demos match the reference frame for frame
Keen 2 proven: all 16 levels match the original to the refresh; Keen 3 at 11 of 16
Keen 1 proven: all 16 levels match the original to the refresh (entering, running, jumping, creatures, shots, dying, the map after)
Keen 1's Border Village matches the original to the refresh: walk in, run, jump, Yorps and Gargs
Keen Dreams v1.93 from your Steam Definitive Edition found and read, title screen included
Export for Android: the files of every found game copied into one folder or ZIP for the phone (the button comes with the launcher)
Keen 3's title sequence matches the original to the refresh
Keen 1's new game and world-map walk match the original to the refresh
Keen 2 and Keen 3 ported; every level of all three episodes plays
Keen 1's and Keen 2's title sequences match the original to the refresh
Keen 1 boots and plays in Megarocket, intro to first level
All seven games' files found and read: Steam, GOG, folders and ZIPs
